deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 154, 1983-84). Grothendieck is building, from a system Σ of pseudo-lines in a projective plane X, a 2-dimensional cell complex 𝒳 (written 𝒳 or 𝔛). In 𝒳:
- the 2-cells are the combinatorial types D of an additional pseudo-line in general position with respect to Σ;
- the oriented edges (D,a) are elementary 'specializations' or 'basculements', where D is pivoted across a vertex of Σ;
- each 2-cell carries a polygonal structure (the cyclic order of its edges);
- there is a rule (point 3) for transporting orientations across edges.
The goal is to obtain a surface, ideally with a natural map 𝒳 → X, that behaves like a projective plane or its double cover. The test is the 'good' local circuits around special vertices: 'superorthogonaux' on the previous page, 'super-singuliers' here.

First half of the page. He finishes analysing the alternative recipe of the previous page: sheets glued by parallel transport, which does give a map 𝒳 → X, though not an immersion. Conclusion:
- the quantity attached to H via 'antiprojections' is the same as before;
- the jumps met along a circuit are the same in both recipes;
- so this recipe is no better for the super-singular circuits.
The fix would be to change 3), using the opposite prescription to fix the orientations, in order to get the correct super-singular circuits. This is an orientation/monodromy sign problem: the local links at the special vertices do not close up correctly.

Second half: the realizable test case. Let Σ = {D_1,…,D_n} be an actual system of straight lines in a real projective plane X. Let δ_i ∈ X^∨ be the dual points.
- Each vertex s_α = D_i ∩ D_j of Σ corresponds to the line Δ_α = δ_iδ_j in X^∨.
- This gives the arrangement Σ̌ of the n(n−1)/2 lines joining the δ_i in pairs.
- Hypotheses: no three δ_i collinear, i.e. Σ simple (no three D_i concurrent). The transcription 'en lignes 3:3' must mean 'non alignés 3 à 3'. Also, after slightly perturbing the δ_i, all vertices of Σ̌ other than the δ_j are simple (double points).
- So Σ̌ has only double points, apart from the 'super-singular' points δ_i, where n−1 lines Δ_α meet.

Dictionary between Σ̌ and the pseudo-lines relative to Σ:
- A face F of Σ̌ ↔ a line D = D_F avoiding all vertices of Σ, whose combinatorial position relative to Σ is constant on F (a generic one-element extension).
- An edge F_α = Δ_α ∩ F̄ ↔ a specialization D → D_α in which the line passes through the vertex s_α. Here s_α is the apex of the corresponding 'specialization triangle' of D, and a_α is the corresponding specialization arc.
- A double point of Σ̌ ↔ a line through two vertices of Σ.
- A point δ_i ↔ the line D_i itself.

So 𝒳 for a realizable Σ should be the cell decomposition of X^∨ given by Σ̌, and the super-singular circuits are the small loops around the δ_i, whose link is a 2(n−1)-gon. The next page uses this to read off the polygonal structure and the transport of orientations. Orientations of F match orientations of D, and transport across a_α matches parallel transport of the orientation of D. The dual picture makes the 'naive' orientation transport plausible, with 𝒳 → X^∨ modelling the realizable case.
errors: The transcription 'les δ_i sont en lignes 3:3 (i.e. Σ stable)' must logically mean 'non alignés 3 à 3 (i.e. Σ simple)', i.e. no three D_i concurrent. Three collinear δ_i would put three Δ-lines through... in fact would make Δ_ij coincide, contradicting the count n(n−1)/2.

Simplicity of the vertices of Σ̌ off the δ_j is not implied by general position of the δ_i: three lines δ_1δ_2, δ_3δ_4, δ_5δ_6 can be concurrent. Grothendieck correctly handles this with 'quitte à perturber un peu'.

The first paragraph's conclusion (same holonomy and jumps as before, hence no improvement) is stated without proof and depends on conventions in point 3) that are only partly legible. It cannot be fully checked from this page.

ideas.what: For a realizable simple line arrangement Σ, the combinatorial types of an added generic line are the faces of the 'dual' arrangement of lines δ_iδ_j through pairs of dual points. Edges are passages through a vertex of Σ, and the points δ_i (where n−1 lines meet) correspond to the lines of Σ themselves.
ideas.modern_name: Extension space / single-element extensions of a rank-3 oriented matroid; arrangement of lines spanned by n points (cf. Goodman–Pollack allowable sequences); related to discriminantal arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Las Vergnas (single-element extensions, 1970s); Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences, ~1980-84); Sturmfels–Ziegler (extension spaces, 1993); Manin–Schechtman (discriminantal arrangements, 1989)

ideas.what: Building a 2-dimensional cell complex of pseudo-lines relative to a pseudo-line system Σ (faces = generic extensions, edges = specializations, polygonal structure, orientation transport). He tests whether it is a surface (projective plane or double cover) by checking the circuits around 'super-singular' vertices, i.e. the lines of Σ themselves.
ideas.modern_name: Topology of the extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid (is it ≃ RP² or S²?)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sturmfels–Ziegler 1993 (extension spaces); Mnëv–Richter-Gebert 1993 (disconnected extension spaces in higher rank)

ideas.what: Orientation-transport conventions (naive/continuous vs parallel vs 'opposite prescription') chosen so that local circuits around special vertices close up correctly, with a natural map 𝒳 → X.
ideas.modern_name: Local orientation/monodromy data on a cell complex; double cover S² → RP² of oriented lines

missed.claim: In 1983-84 Grothendieck was in effect studying the extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid (a pseudo-line arrangement) as a cell complex expected to be a projective plane. He used the dual arrangement of lines through pairs of points as the realizable model. This anticipates by about a decade the Sturmfels–Ziegler extension-space programme and the extension space conjecture. His focus on super-singular circuits (links around the old lines) is exactly where manifoldness has to be checked.
missed.quote: Que se passe-t-il dans le cas où Σ est un syst. de droites dans un plan projectif réel X — quand on regarde les systèmes de droites dans X^∨ correspondant aux sommets de Σ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical precedence point for oriented-matroid theory. His explicit orientation-transport and polygonal-structure formalism may give an alternative combinatorial proof route that rank-3 extension spaces are spheres or projective planes.

missed.claim: He shows that neither proposed orientation-transport recipe yields the correct super-singular circuits. He suggests reversing the prescription in 3), but this is not carried out here.
missed.quote: Il faudrait modifier 3), en prenant la prescription opposée pour définir les trois points d'orientation, pour trouver des bons circuits super singuliers.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of interest for reconstructing his intended proof that the pseudo-line space is a surface. The mathematical question itself is now settled in rank 3 by other methods (to my recollection; unsure of the exact hypotheses).

deep.surprise_reason: The duality model is classical and elementary. What is notable is that Grothendieck, around 1983-84, was independently setting up the extension-space-as-surface problem for pseudo-line arrangements with his own orientation formalism, before the oriented-matroid literature on extension spaces. This is unpublished and little known, but the page itself contains no finished new result.
transcription_corrections: 'mais plus projectif [?] réel^X' should read 'dans un plan projectif réel X'.
'les droites joignant deux : dans les pts δ_i' should read 'les droites joignant deux à deux les pts δ_i'.
'les δ_i sont en lignes 3:3 (i.e. Σ stable)' is likely 'les δ_i sont non alignés 3 à 3 (i.e. Σ simple)'; the inserted words read 'en plus'/'de plus'.
The inserted phrase in the sommets line reads 'distincts des δ_j'; the sentence is: 'les sommets (distincts des δ_j) de ce syst. de n(n−1)/2 droites soient simples'.
'Considérons un point F de Σ̌, par défaut [?] dans une p.' is more plausibly 'Considérons une face F de Σ̌, qui définit une p.d. D = D_F', i.e. a pseudo-line class.
'dit Δ_α, l'arc de spécialisation' is more plausibly 'soit a_α l'arc de spécialisation correspondant'.
First paragraph: 'les sauts des [p.v.?] intervenant dans un circuit sont les mêmes pour les deux' rather than 'par intervention ... des points [?] par les deux'.
